identity.title: Maser emission from the CO envelope of the asymptotic giant branch star W Hydrae

paper_type_evidence.quote: We used high angular resolution observations taken with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) to observe the small-scale structure of CO $J=3-2$ emission around the oxygen-rich AGB star W Hya.

evidence.quote: W Hya is a semi-regular variable star located at $\approx 100$ pc from the Sun (cite: Vlemmings03; vanLeeuwen2007)

question.value: Is there CO maser emission in the J=3-2 line around the AGB star W Hya, where does it come from, and what pumps it

evidence.quote: While radiative transfer models have shown that molecular levels of CO can become mildly inverted, causing maser emission, CO maser emission has yet to be confirmed observationally.
Here we present the first unambiguous detection of CO maser emission, in the $J=3-2$ transition, around the oxygen-rich AGB star W Hya.

claims.hypothesis: CO J=3-2 emission around W Hya contains unambiguous maser emission
claims.experiment: High angular resolution ALMA band 7 observations at two epochs, continuum-subtracted CO J=3-2 maps and single-beam spectra
claims.result: Peak Tb about 1950 K above the 2700 K stellar continuum in both epochs, implying tau of about -0.55
claims.finding: First unambiguous detection of CO maser emission, amplifying the stellar continuum

evidence.quote: As the emission is amplifying the underlying stellar continuum, the brightness temperatures imply a maser optical depth of $\tau\approx-0.55$.
Here we present the first unambiguous detection of CO maser emission, in the $J=3-2$ transition, around the oxygen-rich AGB star W Hya.

claims.hypothesis: The maser changes with time and with background structure
claims.experiment: Compared the two epochs (2015, 2017) and imaged three days of epoch 1 separately with a common beam
claims.result: Morphology changed markedly between epochs; Tb varied between about 1330 K and 2000 K over five days while the continuum varied by less than 2.5%
claims.finding: Changes reflect the underlying stellar and extended-atmosphere structure and small foreground masing changes

evidence.quote: This indicates that there could be variability of the order of $\pm20\%$ within only a five-day timescale.
Thus, we suggest that the changes in the maser emission primarily reflect changes in the underlying structure of the star and extended atmosphere.

claims.hypothesis: The 4.6 micron continuum radiation (dust) can pump the CO J=3-2 maser
claims.experiment: 1-D Monte Carlo CO radiative transfer with the 4.6 micron field boosted by a factor M and with an added dust shell
claims.result: M~3 and adjusted V0, beta, Vt reproduce the maser, requiring a dust shell of tau(4.6 micron)~0.2 that conflicts with the observed infrared spectrum
claims.finding: Continuum pumping by dust is not a viable explanation

evidence.quote: Although the model results show that the maser can be reproduced by a general increase in IR radiation field and fine-tuning the model parameters, we conclude that this is not a viable solution.

claims.hypothesis: Line overlap of absorption and emission lines near 4.6 micron pumps the maser
claims.experiment: Changed the relative radiation field seen by individual v=0-1 IR lines in the model
claims.result: Maser J=3-2 inversion produced by selective pumping, consistent with the estimated mass-loss rates of W Hya; the pump cannot be uniquely constrained from one transition
claims.finding: Line overlap is highly likely the main pumping mechanism; multi-transition observations are needed

evidence.quote: it is highly likely that the line overlap is the main reason for the observed CO maser.
However, a detailed study of this would involve too many degenerate parameters to be constrained with a single observed maser transition.

evidence.quote: In order to investigate the occurrence of the CO maser in the $J=3-2$ transition, we perform one-dimensional radiative transfer models

evidence.quote: we conclude that this is not a viable solution. We thus investigate pumping that can occur due to line overlap around 4.6 $\mu$m.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Transverse motions of dense clumps across the stellar disk rejected as the cause of the morphology change (would need ~10 km/s)

evidence.quote: transverse motions of dense clumps across the full stellar disk within two years would, at the distance of W Hya, require a transverse velocity of $\sim10$ km s$^{-1}$
